note: PLACEHOLDER. Every params object here validates against the published race_opponent_summary manifest input_schema (additionalProperties: false, $refs inlined the way publish_experiments.py inlines them), and every value is plausible, but nobody has dispatched one. So a verdict drawn from this list is a claim about the pipeline, not about the agent. EIGHT cases, and DEFAULT_JUDGE_CONFIG.gates.minCases is 20. A corpus verdict over this list therefore resolves CAN'T SAY however the judge voted, because the floor was set from measured agent non-determinism and eight runs measure that rather than the branch. Eight is deliberate and not a rounding error: one clean baseline plus seven single-axis variations is what one change can author honestly across nine agents. Whether to grow every list to 20 or to lower the floor is still open — do not read the shortfall as a decision. Varied along: how much collected text there is to structure, which is the only input that can raise or lower output quality here — two full sources per opponent, a single source, one-sentence stubs, and an opponent whose sources array is empty, which the schema explicitly allows and which should contribute no groundable sections rather than an invented one; which source types are present, since a Ballotpedia page and a campaign site say different things about the same person; field size, one to three opponents, because threat tiers are relative; and whether the candidate platform is full, bio-only, or absent, which is what decides whether issue contrasts can exist at all. People are fictional placeholders in the house style (gp-webapp e2e-tests briefings.spec.ts uses 'Test Official'); this file is public, so no real person is named. States, cities, office titles and L2 voter file column names are real.

sources.text: Test Incumbent (Minneapolis, Minnesota) is a member of the Minneapolis City Council, representing Ward 3. They assumed office in 2022. Their current term ends in January 2027. Test Incumbent ran for re-election to the Minneapolis City Council to represent Ward 3. They advanced from the primary on August 11, 2026. Prior to election, Test Incumbent worked as a transportation planner for a regional council of governments. Education: B.A. in urban studies.

About — Test Incumbent has spent four years on the council fighting for a Ward 3 that working families can afford to stay in. Priorities: pass the inclusionary zoning update with no density bonus loopholes; fund the pedestrian safety plan at the level the plan itself calls for; and hold the line on the property tax levy while protecting library hours. Endorsed by the regional building trades council and two neighborhood associations.

Test Challenger is a small business owner running for the Minneapolis City Council in Ward 3. After eleven years running a hardware store on the avenue, Test Challenger is running on three commitments: a permitting process that answers in ten business days, a police staffing plan with published response-time targets by neighborhood, and no new street assessments on commercial frontage without a vote of the affected owners.

candidate_platform.bio: I taught eighth-grade science in this city for twelve years and chaired my neighborhood association land-use committee for four. I am running because the people who are priced out of this ward never get asked what would have kept them here.

issues.title: Housing affordability
issues.description: Rent stabilization on buildings over twenty units, and no density bonus that does not produce units at sixty percent of area median income.

issues.title: Transit reliability
issues.description: Restore fifteen-minute headways on the two busiest bus lines before any new capital project is funded.
